newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivia postpones YPFB privatization to Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia postpones YPFB privatization to Dec 5.

text.p: Bolivia has decided to postpone the privatization of oil and gas firm Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB) until December 5 from October 31, Capitalization Secretary Carlos Saravia said Friday.
He also told reporters that the firm has a book value of $880 million, including net assets valued at $470 million and debts of $410 million which must be assumed by the eventual private buyers.

"On the request of several interested companies, the presentation, opening and adjudication of the economic proposals for the capitalization of the three YPFB units has been postponed until December 5," Saravia told reporters.

He added that the key issue of rules governing hydrocarbon transport fees had been resolved: "During visits to companies over the last week the government has communicated the rules governing hydrocarbon transport fees, which was the issue that still had to be cleared up."
The sale of YPFB was originally scheduled for July 1995 and has been postponed several times.
Saravia said that the government expected bidders to at least match the firm's book value: "That is the base upon which the capitalization must be carried out."

Twenty-two international firms have prequalified to bid for a 50-percent share in YPFB, which will be sold off in three parts. Two of the units will become competing exploration and production companies, while the third will be a transport firm. A fourth services and marketing unit will remain in government hands.
The plans to sell YPFB have generated great controversy and had a stormy ride through Congress.
